$comment: Make the model libraries this artifact already ships reachable from an imported SPICE netlist.
$shape: repairs[].edits[].find must occur exactly once in its file; both repairs are insertions, so each declares a marker (a string that is absent before and present exactly once after).
$mechanism: The File menu exposes Import SPICE as <input type=file multiple>, and that is the only way files can enter this deployment: webkitdirectory occurs nowhere in the build, so every selected file arrives with an empty webkitRelativePath and the importer falls back to File.name.

A flattened selection cannot express a directory, but the resolver is written as though it could: Jl() rejects anything that climbs above dirname(entry), which is empty for a flat name. So .include ../models/cap.lib -- the spelling cap.lib and opamp.lib both instruct the user to write -- is refused as SPICE_SOURCE_INCLUDE_DENIED before the file pool is consulted, and .include cap.lib without also selecting cap.lib is SPICE_SOURCE_INCLUDE_MISSING. Measured in a real browser by scripts/spice-import.mjs, whose fixtures are those three spellings plus one library this build does not ship.

Edit 1 adds the shipped libraries to the pool Zl() is handed. Edit 2 lets a relative include whose strict resolution failed fall back to its filename. A library this build does not ship still fails, which is what keeps the change scoped.
Precedence: a file the user selected always wins -- the pool skips any name the selection already carries, and the fallback only runs when the strict answer failed or is absent from the pool.

Risk, stated because it is a real behaviour change: when a netlist includes a library the user did not supply, the bundled one is used, silently from the deck's point of view. If the two define different devices under the same subcircuit name, the simulation that follows is not the one the netlist intended. That is why the libraries are the ones this build ships and calls educational, and why the alternative -- a hard refusal -- is what the product does today.
Nothing here adds a network target, so the egress surface (check 9) is unchanged; the pool is text already inside the shell.

repairs.why: offer the shipped model libraries to the importer, so an .include the user cannot supply still resolves

var BUILTIN_SOURCE_LIBS=[{"name":"cap.lib","text":"* Educational capacitor roles for VREF (ideal C; Level-1 discovery)
* Shared by netlists via:  .include ../models/cap.lib
*
* Role subcircuits (prefer these over bare C* when documenting intent):
*
*   cap_out     Cout — VREF / load decoupling (p→n typically vref→0)
*   cap_comp    Cc  — miller / mid-node compensation (e.g. vx→vref)
*   cap_bypass  supply or bias-node bypass
*
* Technology tags (same ideal C; name encodes foundry intent only):
*
*   cap_mim     MIM-style dense film cap
*   cap_mom     MOM / fringe metal cap
*
* Instantiate with size override, e.g.:
*   Xcout vref 0   cap_out  c={Cout}
*   Xcc   vx   vref cap_comp c={Cc}
*   Xdec  vdd  0   cap_bypass c=10p
*
* Defaults match typical scm_cout / 2t_cout educational decks (Cout=200p, Cc=2p).

.subckt cap_out p n params: c=200p
C1 p n {c}
.ends cap_out

.subckt cap_comp p n params: c=2p
C1 p n {c}
.ends cap_comp

.subckt cap_bypass p n params: c=10p
C1 p n {c}
.ends cap_bypass

.subckt cap_mim p n params: c=200p
C1 p n {c}
.ends cap_mim

.subckt cap_mom p n params: c=2p
C1 p n {c}
.ends cap_mom
"},{"name":"opamp.lib","text":"* Behavioral idea opamps for ngspice (educational)
* Shared by netlists via:  .include ../models/opamp.lib
*
* Subcircuits:
*   opamp_se    diff-in → single-ended out   pins: inp inm out vdd vss
*   opamp_diff  diff-in → differential out   pins: inp inm outp outm vdd vss
*
* Defaults = recommended **non-ideal** set for ~1.8 V CMOS / IoT VREF.
* Override per instance, e.g.:
*   X1 inp inm out vdd 0 opamp_se av0=1e6 vos=0 rout=1m
*
* Ideal quick set:
*   av0=1e6 gbw=100meg rin=1T rout=1m vos=0 acm=0 swing=10

* =====================================================================
* SE: soft-rail tanh + dominant pole (fp = gbw/av0), Rout series.
* Midrail tracks (vdd+vss)/2. CMRR ≈ av0/acm (default ~60 dB).
* =====================================================================
.subckt opamp_se inp inm out vdd vss params: av0=10k gbw=1meg rin=100meg rout=10k vos=1m acm=10 swing=0.9
.param pi=3.141592653589793
.param fp={gbw/av0}
.param rpole=1k
.param cpole={1/(2*pi*fp*rpole)}
*
Rin inp inm {rin}
*
Bclip outi 0 V={ 0.5*(v(vdd)+v(vss)) + swing*tanh( av0*( (v(inp)-v(inm)-vos) + (acm/av0)*(0.5*(v(inp)+v(inm))-0.5*(v(vdd)+v(vss))) ) /(swing+1p) ) }
*
Rpole outi pole {rpole}
Cpole pole 0 {cpole}
Rout pole out {rout}
.ends opamp_se

* =====================================================================
* DIFF: Vod soft-limited about vocm; Acm*Vic shifts both outs (output CM).
* Differential CMRR is high; set acm to model output-CM CM sensitivity.
* =====================================================================
.subckt opamp_diff inp inm outp outm vdd vss params: av0=10k gbw=1meg rin=100meg rout=10k vos=1m acm=10 vocm=0.9 swing=0.9
.param pi=3.141592653589793
.param fp={gbw/av0}
.param rpole=1k
.param cpole={1/(2*pi*fp*rpole)}
*
Rin inp inm {rin}
*
Bclip vod_raw 0 V={ (2*swing)*tanh( av0*(v(inp)-v(inm)-vos)/(2*swing+1p) ) }
Rpole vod_raw vod_f {rpole}
Cpole vod_f 0 {cpole}
*
Bcm cm 0 V={acm * ( 0.5*(v(inp)+v(inm)) - vocm )}
*
Bop outpi 0 V={vocm + 0.5*v(vod_f) + v(cm)}
Bom outmi 0 V={vocm - 0.5*v(vod_f) + v(cm)}
Routp outpi outp {rout}
Routm outmi outm {rout}
.ends opamp_diff
"},{"name":"cmos.lib","text":"* Educational CMOS Level-1 (Shichman–Hodges) + BJT — browser SPICE profile
* Included as: .include "/spice-simulator/models/cmos.lib"
*
* MOSFET: nmos_rvt pmos_rvt nmos_nat nmos_dep nmos_hvt pmos_hvt nmos_tox pmos_tox
* BJT: npn_l1 pnp_l1
* Teaching context: L ≈ 0.18 µm, VDD ≈ 1.8 V (thin ox).

*
* Process corners -- TEACHING-GRADE, not a PDK corner
* ---------------------------------------------------
*   __cn_sel = -1   ff  (fast)
*   __cn_sel =  0   tt  (typical)  <- declared at the bottom of this header
*   __cn_sel = +1   ss  (slow)
*
* A made-up spread on the Level-1 parameters, meant to show WHICH WAY a bias
* point moves between corners, not to predict a real process. Do not read it
* as SKY130 or as any foundry corner. Slow means |VTO| rises, KP falls and
* current gain falls; fast is the reverse.
*
* WHY A SELECTOR RATHER THAN A .lib SECTION. The deck assembler includes this
* file with .include, and the executor writes ngbehavior=lt into spinit.
* Under that behaviour ngspice rewrites the .lib directive with a section
* argument into a plain include of the whole file plus an include of the
* section name as if it were a filename, so sectioned libraries cannot work
* here at all -- measured against the shipped engine, not assumed. Re-declaring
* a .model is no better: ngspice keeps the FIRST definition and reports
* nothing, so a deck cannot override this file from below. What does work is
* a parameter the deck redefines after the include, because parameters,
* unlike models, are last-wins. That is the whole mechanism: one selector,
* one expression per spread parameter, and the deck writes the selector only
* when it means to.
*
* The selector line is emitted only for a named corner other than the typical
* one, so a run that names no corner produces exactly the deck this library
* produced before the corners existed. The spread parameters do reach the
* solver through the expression evaluator rather than the literal parser, and
* on a ten-device test circuit that path is worth up to 2e-13 relative, on the
* collector current of the BJT leg. Measured, not assumed: an otherwise
* identical literal copy of these same numbers agrees with this file to 1.9e-13,
* and that literal copy run against itself agrees exactly, which is how the
* expression path rather than the numbers was identified as the cause. Twelve
* orders of magnitude below the smallest corner shift declared here.
*
* BJT IS and BF are spread too, deliberately: a corner that ignored half the
* library would turn "sweep the corners on a BJT circuit" into three identical
* answers, which is worse than not offering the corner at all.
.param __cn_sel = 0

.model nmos_rvt NMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={0.5+0.08*__cn_sel} KP={200u-30u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model pmos_rvt PMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={-0.5-0.08*__cn_sel} KP={100u-15u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model nmos_nat NMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={0.0+0.08*__cn_sel} KP={200u-30u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model nmos_dep NMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={-0.7+0.08*__cn_sel} KP={200u-30u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model nmos_hvt NMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={0.7+0.08*__cn_sel} KP={200u-30u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model pmos_hvt PMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={-0.7-0.08*__cn_sel} KP={100u-15u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model nmos_tox NMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={0.7+0.08*__cn_sel} KP={80u-12u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model pmos_tox PMOS LEVEL=1 VTO={-0.7-0.08*__cn_sel} KP={40u-6u*__cn_sel} GAMMA=0.4 PHI=0.7 LAMBDA=0.05
.model npn_l1 NPN IS={1e-16*(1-0.25*__cn_sel)} BF={100*(1-0.15*__cn_sel)} NF=1 VAF=50 IKF=1e-2
.model pnp_l1 PNP IS={1e-16*(1-0.25*__cn_sel)} BF={50*(1-0.15*__cn_sel)} NF=1 VAF=30 IKF=5e-3
"}];function builtinSourceFiles(e){let t=new Set;for(let n of e)t.add(Kl(n.path));return BUILTIN_SOURCE_LIBS.filter(n=>!t.has(n.name)).map(n=>({path:n.name,bytes:new TextEncoder().encode(n.text)}))}async function Ql(e,t){let n=Kl(t)??t,r=await Zl([...e,...builtinSourceFiles(e)])
